<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917769_theRebbe_254" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917769_theRebbe_254__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">11 Nissan 5731</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the name of the tribe Asher, its connection to Israel's praise and redemption, and raises questions about the nature of choice between Israel and G-d.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"On the eleventh day, the prince of the children of Asher [offered]."</t>
    <t s="1">And it is brought in the Midrash:</t>
    <t s="2">All the tribes were named for the sake of Israel's redemption and for their praise.</t>
    <t s="3">And Asher was named for the sake of Israel's redemption, as it is said:</t>
    <t s="4">"And all nations shall call you fortunate, for you shall be a desirable land, says the L-rd of Hosts."</t>
    <t s="5">And for their praise, as it is said:</t>
    <t s="6">"Fortunate is the people for whom it is so; fortunate is the people whose G-d is the L-rd."</t>
    <t s="7">The good fortune of Israel is only because they chose the Holy One, blessed be He, to be their G-d.</t>
    <t s="8">And the Holy One, blessed be He, chose them to be His treasured people.</t>
    <t s="9">Therefore, when the prince of Asher came to offer,</t>
    <t s="10">he offered his sacrifice regarding the choice that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose Israel from among all the nations,</t>
    <t s="11">as it is said:</t>
    <t s="12">"And the L-rd your G-d has chosen you to be His treasured people."</t>
    <t s="13">And it needs to be understood:</t>
    <t s="14">For at the beginning of the matter, it says that Israel's good fortune is that they chose the Holy One, blessed be He</t>
    <t s="15">(and that He then chose them seems to be an additional matter).</t>
    <t s="16">And afterwards it says that Asher</t>
    <t s="17">(for the name of Israel's good fortune)</t>
    <t s="18">offered his sacrifice regarding the choice that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose Israel.</t>
    <t s="19">Also, it needs to be understood:</t>
    <t s="20">Choice applies specifically to two things that are equal,</t>
    <t s="21">or where each has a virtue that the other lacks.</t>
    <t s="22">But regarding the Holy One, blessed be He, and, by contrast, the alien gods,</t>
    <t s="23">how can it be said that Israel chose the Holy One, blessed be He?</t>
    <t s="24">And similarly, regarding the Holy One, blessed be He, choosing Israel,</t>
    <t s="25">Israel is incomparably superior to all the nations,</t>
    <t s="26">so what is the meaning of the Holy One, blessed be He, choosing Israel?</t>
    <t s="27">Also, what is said in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="28">that "You have chosen us from every people and tongue" refers to the physical body, which in its materiality resembles the bodies of the nations of the world,</t>
    <t s="29">requires explanation,</t>
    <t s="30">for that the body of Israel resembles</t>
    <t s="31">(externally)</t>
    <t s="32">the bodies of the nations of the world is not an explanation</t>
    <t s="33">(apparently)</t>
    <t s="34">regarding the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the Midrashic parable of the king and the wise man, questioning why special cleverness is needed to choose the king over the changing officials.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what is said,</t>
    <t s="2">"The L-rd is my portion, said my soul."</t>
    <t s="3">And it is brought in the Midrash:</t>
    <t s="4">A parable of a king who entered a province, and with him were dukes, governors, and generals, etc.</t>
    <t s="5">One said, "I will take the dukes for myself"; another said, "I will take the governors for myself"; another said, "I will take the generals for myself."</t>
    <t s="6">There was one clever person there who said, "I will take the king for myself, for all of them are replaceable, but the king is not replaceable."</t>
    <t s="7">So too, the nations of the world—some worship the sun, some worship the moon, etc., but Israel worships only the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="8">Thus it is said, "The L-rd is my portion, said my soul."</t>
    <t s="9">And the precise point in this is known,</t>
    <t s="10">for apparently,</t>
    <t s="11">even one who is not clever, and even a small child,</t>
    <t s="12">knows that the king is greater than the dukes, etc.</t>
    <t s="13">So why is cleverness needed to choose the king?</t>
    <t s="14">And also,</t>
    <t s="15">even if the dukes, etc., were not replaceable, it would be simply understood that the king is greater than them.</t>
    <t s="16">[And especially according to what is known</t>
    <t s="17">in the explanation of the verse,</t>
    <t s="18">"From his shoulder and upward he was taller than all the people,"</t>
    <t s="19">that even the shoulder of the king,</t>
    <t s="20">meaning the attributes that are drawn from the intellect of the head and below it,</t>
    <t s="21">is higher than the head</t>
    <t s="22">(the intellect)</t>
    <t s="23">of all the people,</t>
    <t s="24">in which</t>
    <t s="25">(all the people)</t>
    <t s="26">are included even the greatest ministers],</t>
    <t s="27">so why</t>
    <t s="28">is the reason needed that "all of them are replaceable"?</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
